questions.stem: What is the average time complexity for searching a key in a balanced BST?
questions.explanation: In a balanced binary search tree (BST), the height of the tree is logarithmic relative to the number of nodes, $n$. This means that operations such as searching, which involve traversing from the root to a leaf, take $O(\\log n)$ time on average. The most tempting wrong option might be $O(n)$, which would be the case for an unbalanced BST, but not for a balanced one.

questions.stem: Which node is used to replace a node with two children during deletion in a BST?
questions.explanation: When deleting a node with two children in a BST, the in-order predecessor or successor is used to replace the node. This ensures that the BST properties are maintained, as the in-order predecessor is the largest node in the left subtree and the in-order successor is the smallest node in the right subtree. The option of using any leaf node is incorrect because it would not necessarily preserve the BST invariant.

questions.stem: What happens to a BST when elements are inserted in random order?

options.text: It always becomes a perfectly balanced tree.
It may become balanced, but not guaranteed.
It always degenerates into a linked list.

Random insertion can sometimes lead to a balanced tree, but it can also result in an unbalanced tree depending on the order of insertion. The option suggesting it always becomes a perfectly balanced tree is incorrect because balancing is not guaranteed without specific balancing operations.

questions.stem: Describe the process of deleting a node with one child in a BST.
markingGuide: Identify that the child node replaces the node to be deleted.

questions.explanation: When deleting a node with one child, the child node takes the place of the node to be deleted. This maintains the BST invariant as the child is either greater or less than the parent, depending on its position. The parent node is re-linked to the child node.

questions.stem: Which of the following operations can degrade to $O(n)$ time complexity in a BST?

This occurs when elements are inserted in a sorted order, causing the tree to lose its balanced structure. Therefore, all these operations can potentially degrade to $O(n)$ in the worst-case scenario.

questions.stem: Calculate the number of nodes in a complete BST of height 3.
questions.explanation: A complete BST of height 3 has $2^{h+1} - 1 = 2^4 - 1 = 15$ nodes, where $h$ is the height of the tree.
